name: SQL tests · Health and hospitals (20 tables, 212 queries, 32 scripts)

tables.name: hospitals
tables.description: Healthcare centres of the system: they group services, rooms and staff.

tables.name: specialties
tables.description: Medical and surgical specialties recognised by the hospital.

fields.name: needs_icu
fields.description: Does it need an intensive care unit?

tables.name: services
tables.description: Clinical services of every hospital; they link a hospital and a specialty.

tables.name: doctors
tables.description: Medical staff: every doctor has a specialty, a service and a category.

fields.name: is_researcher
fields.description: Does the doctor take part in research?

fields.name: hired_date
fields.description: Date the doctor joined the system

tables.name: nurses
tables.description: Nursing staff assigned to a service and to a shift.

fields.name: is_supervisor
fields.description: Is the nurse a shift supervisor?

tables.name: insurers
tables.description: Health insurers and the percentage of coverage they offer.

tables.name: patients
tables.description: People treated in the system, with their insurer and demographic data.

fields.name: id_insurer
fields.description: Insurer of the patient (may be missing)

fields.name: is_chronic
fields.description: Does the patient have a chronic disease?

tables.name: rooms
tables.description: Rooms and admission boxes of every hospital.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Type: Single, Double, ICU or Isolation

fields.name: has_bathroom
fields.description: Does it have its own bathroom?

tables.name: admissions
tables.description: Hospital stays: they link patient, room and the doctor in charge.

fields.name: is_emergency
fields.description: Was the patient admitted through the emergency department?

fields.name: expected_days
fields.description: Expected length of stay in days (may be missing)

tables.name: appointments
tables.description: Appointment schedule: patient, doctor, date, status and room.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Status: Pending, Attended, Cancelled or No-show

tables.name: visits
tables.description: Visits actually carried out; they may come from an appointment or be walk-ins.

fields.name: id_appointment
fields.description: Appointment it comes from (null if the patient walked in)

fields.name: cost
fields.description: Cost of the visit in euros

tables.name: diagnoses
tables.description: Catalogue of diagnoses (ICD-10 code) with severity and specialty.

tables.name: visit_diagnoses
tables.description: Resolves the M:N relationship between visits and diagnoses (main diagnosis plus secondary ones).

tables.name: drugs
tables.description: Catalogue of drugs with price, route of administration and stock.

tables.name: treatments
tables.description: Treatments prescribed to a patient by a doctor from a diagnosis.

tables.name: prescriptions
tables.description: Prescription lines: which drugs every treatment includes (M:N).

tables.name: surgeries
tables.description: Surgical operations performed, with surgeon, risk and cost.

fields.name: id_admission
fields.description: Linked admission (null if it was outpatient)

tables.name: allergies
tables.description: Known allergies of every patient (to a drug or to a substance).

fields.name: id_drug
fields.description: Drug that causes it (null if not applicable)

tables.name: labs
tables.description: Laboratory results (blood or urine) with their values and whether they are abnormal.

fields.name: cholesterol
fields.description: Total cholesterol in mg/dL (may be missing)

tables.name: invoices
tables.description: Health billing, linked to an admission or to an appointment.

queries.name: A01 · All specialties
queries.description: SELECT * on specialties, ordered by identifier.
queries.sql: SELECT * FROM specialties ORDER BY id_specialty

queries.name: A02 · Hospitals: beds in hundreds
queries.description: Projection with aliases and arithmetic: numeric division and order by beds.
queries.sql: SELECT name AS hospital, city, num_beds / 100 AS beds_hundreds FROM hospitals ORDER BY num_beds DESC

queries.name: A03 · Large hospitals (>= 800 beds)
queries.description: Numeric filter with >= and a double order.
queries.sql: SELECT name, num_beds, level FROM hospitals WHERE num_beds >= 800 ORDER BY num_beds DESC, name

queries.name: A04 · University hospitals with a phone
queries.description: Boolean filter combined with IS NOT NULL.
queries.sql: SELECT id_hospital, name, city FROM hospitals WHERE is_university = true AND phone IS NOT NULL ORDER BY name

queries.name: A05 · Patients without a phone
queries.description: Missing values are asked with IS NULL.
queries.sql: SELECT id_patient, name, last_name, city FROM patients WHERE phone IS NULL ORDER BY last_name, name

queries.name: A06 · Doctor emails in upper case
queries.description: UPPER on a field that may be missing: the rows with a null email are filtered out.
queries.sql: SELECT name, last_name, UPPER(email) AS email FROM doctors WHERE email IS NOT NULL ORDER BY last_name, name

queries.name: A07 · Last names that start with G
queries.description: LIKE with a wildcard at the end.
queries.sql: SELECT name, last_name FROM doctors WHERE last_name LIKE 'G%' ORDER BY last_name, name

queries.name: A08 · Drugs that do not start with A
queries.description: LIKE combined with NOT.
queries.sql: SELECT name, active_ingredient, price FROM drugs WHERE name NOT LIKE 'A%' ORDER BY name

queries.name: A09 · Surgeries of high or medium risk
queries.description: Membership of a list with IN.
queries.sql: SELECT name, risk, cost FROM surgeries WHERE risk IN ('high', 'medium') ORDER BY cost DESC

queries.name: A10 · Specialties that are neither Central nor Surgical
queries.description: NOT IN on the area.
queries.sql: SELECT name, area, residency_years FROM specialties WHERE area NOT IN ('Central', 'Surgical') ORDER BY name

queries.name: A11 · Lab tests with glucose between 100 and 200
queries.description: Range with BETWEEN (endpoints included).
queries.sql: SELECT id_lab, glucose, cholesterol FROM labs WHERE glucose BETWEEN 100 AND 200 ORDER BY glucose DESC LIMIT 15

queries.name: A12 · Emergency admissions with 2 to 5 expected days
queries.description: BETWEEN combined with a boolean filter.
queries.sql: SELECT id_admission, reason, expected_days, cost_per_day FROM admissions WHERE is_emergency = true AND expected_days BETWEEN 2 AND 5 ORDER BY expected_days, cost_per_day DESC LIMIT 20

queries.name: A13 · Doctor categories (DISTINCT)
queries.description: Distinct values of a column.
queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT category FROM doctors ORDER BY category

queries.name: A14 · Appointment types and statuses (DISTINCT of two columns)
queries.description: Distinct combinations of type and status.
queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT type, status FROM appointments ORDER BY type, status

queries.name: A15 · Billing totals
queries.description: COUNT, SUM, MIN, MAX and a rounded AVG.
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS invoices, SUM(amount) AS total, MIN(amount) AS min, MAX(amount) AS max, ROUND(AVG(amount), 2) AS avg FROM invoices

queries.name: A16 · Invoices by payment method
queries.description: Grouping with COUNT, including the null group.
queries.sql: SELECT COALESCE(payment_method, 'no method') AS method, COUNT(*) AS invoices, SUM(amount) AS total FROM invoices GROUP BY payment_method ORDER BY total DESC

queries.name: A17 · Appointments by status
queries.description: GROUP BY and ORDER BY descending.
queries.sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS appointments FROM appointments GROUP BY status ORDER BY appointments DESC, status

queries.name: A18 · Appointment statuses with more than 10 appointments
queries.description: Filtering groups with HAVING.
queries.sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS appointments FROM appointments GROUP BY status HAVING COUNT(*) > 10 ORDER BY appointments DESC

queries.name: A19 · Patients with three or more admissions
queries.description: HAVING on a patient-admission join.
queries.sql: SELECT p.id_patient, p.name, p.last_name, COUNT(*) AS admissions FROM patients AS p INNER JOIN admissions AS i ON i.id_patient = p.id_patient GROUP BY p.id_patient, p.name, p.last_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ORDER BY admissions DESC, p.last_name

queries.name: A20 · Patients by the initial of the last name
queries.description: GROUP BY with a text function.
queries.sql: SELECT SUBSTR(last_name, 1, 1) AS initial, COUNT(*) AS patients FROM patients GROUP BY SUBSTR(last_name, 1, 1) ORDER BY initial

queries.name: A21 · Glucose of one patient, from highest to lowest
queries.description: ORDER BY descending with an explicit NULLS LAST.
queries.sql: SELECT id_lab, date, glucose FROM labs WHERE id_patient = 3 ORDER BY glucose DESC NULLS LAST, date

queries.name: A22 · Glucose of one patient, from lowest to highest
queries.description: With ASC the nulls come first by default.
queries.sql: SELECT id_lab, glucose FROM labs WHERE id_patient = 7 ORDER BY glucose, id_lab

queries.name: A23 · Oldest patients, page 2
queries.description: LIMIT/OFFSET on an order by date of birth.
queries.sql: SELECT name, last_name, birth_date FROM patients ORDER BY birth_date LIMIT 6 OFFSET 6

queries.name: A24 · Four patients from the eighth on
queries.description: MySQL style LIMIT skip, n.
queries.sql: SELECT id_patient, name FROM patients ORDER BY id_patient LIMIT 7, 4

queries.name: A25 · Record of three patients
queries.description: Concatenation with || and text functions.
queries.sql: SELECT UPPER(last_name) || ', ' || name AS record, city, blood_group FROM patients WHERE id_patient IN (1, 2, 3) ORDER BY id_patient

queries.name: A26 · Missing values: COALESCE and ROUND
queries.description: COALESCE with a default value, plus NULLIF and ROUND.
queries.sql: SELECT id_lab, COALESCE(glucose, -1) AS glucose, IFNULL(cholesterol, 0) AS cholesterol FROM labs WHERE glucose IS NULL OR cholesterol IS NULL ORDER BY id_lab

queries.name: A27 · Normalised insurer phone
queries.description: IFNULL + TRIM + NULLIF to leave the empty phones as null.
queries.sql: SELECT name, NULLIF(TRIM(IFNULL(phone, '')), '') AS phone FROM insurers ORDER BY id_insurer

queries.name: A28 · Oral drugs against the rest
queries.description: The <> operator and NOT.
queries.sql: SELECT name, route FROM drugs WHERE NOT route = 'oral' ORDER BY route, name

queries.name: A29 · No appointment lasts more than two hours
queries.description: A query without results: rowCount 0.
queries.sql: SELECT id_appointment, duration_min FROM appointments WHERE duration_min > 120

queries.name: A30 · Average price by presentation
queries.description: HAVING and order by an alias.
queries.sql: SELECT presentation, COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND(AVG(price), 2) AS avg_price FROM drugs GROUP BY presentation HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY avg_price DESC

queries.name: A31 · Patients and emails by city
queries.description: Implicit join with commas: patients and their insurer.
queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS patient, s.name AS insurance FROM patients AS p, insurers AS s WHERE p.id_insurer = s.id_insurer AND p.city = 'Madrid' ORDER BY p.last_name

queries.name: A32 · Patients by blood group
queries.description: GROUP BY counting the unknown group as well.
queries.sql: SELECT COALESCE(blood_group, 'unknown') AS blood_group, COUNT(*) AS patients FROM patients GROUP BY blood_group ORDER BY patients DESC

queries.name: A33 · Nurses by shift
queries.description: Simple grouping with an implicit DISTINCT.
queries.sql: SELECT shift, COUNT(*) AS nurses, ROUND(AVG(years_experience), 1) AS avg_experience FROM nurses GROUP BY shift ORDER BY nurses DESC

queries.name: A34 · Rooms with a bathroom and more than one bed
queries.description: Two boolean filters and a numeric one.
queries.sql: SELECT code, type, num_beds FROM rooms WHERE has_bathroom = true AND num_beds > 1 ORDER BY num_beds DESC, code

queries.name: A35 · Chronic diagnoses, moderate or severe
queries.description: Filter combined with AND.
queries.sql: SELECT code, name, severity FROM diagnoses WHERE is_chronic = true AND severity <> 'mild' ORDER BY name

queries.name: A36 · Successful surgeries by operating room
queries.description: GROUP BY with SUM and AVG.
queries.sql: SELECT operating_room, COUNT(*) AS surgeries, SUM(cost) AS total_cost, ROUND(AVG(duration_min), 0) AS avg_duration FROM surgeries WHERE successful = true GROUP BY operating_room ORDER BY total_cost DESC

queries.name: A37 · Drugs with low stock
queries.description: Numeric threshold and ascending order.
queries.sql: SELECT name, stock, price FROM drugs WHERE stock <= 150 ORDER BY stock

queries.name: A38 · Veteran doctors who do not do research
queries.description: Two conditions with NOT.
queries.sql: SELECT name, last_name, years_experience, category FROM doctors WHERE years_experience > 20 AND NOT is_researcher ORDER BY years_experience DESC

queries.name: A39 · Insurers with high coverage
queries.description: Numeric and boolean filter.
queries.sql: SELECT name, type, coverage_percent FROM insurers WHERE coverage_percent >= 80 ORDER BY coverage_percent DESC

queries.name: A40 · Severe allergies
queries.description: Text and date filter.
queries.sql: SELECT id_allergy, substance, severity, detected_date FROM allergies WHERE severity = 'severe' ORDER BY detected_date DESC

queries.name: A41 · Longest diagnosis names
queries.description: ORDER BY of a text function.
queries.sql: SELECT code, name, LENGTH(name) AS letters FROM diagnoses ORDER BY letters DESC, code LIMIT 8

queries.name: A42 · ICD code by prefix
queries.description: SUBSTR to extract the first letter.
queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT SUBSTR(code, 1, 1) AS letter FROM diagnoses ORDER BY letter

queries.name: A43 · Patients with specific blood groups
queries.description: IN on text.
queries.sql: SELECT name, last_name, blood_group FROM patients WHERE blood_group IN ('O-', 'AB+', 'A-') ORDER BY blood_group, last_name

queries.name: A44 · Appointments in the first half of 2025
queries.description: BETWEEN on dates stored as text.
queries.sql: SELECT id_appointment, date, time, type FROM appointments WHERE date BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-06-30' ORDER BY date, time LIMIT 20

queries.name: A45 · Patients without a blood group
queries.description: IS NULL and ORDER BY.
queries.sql: SELECT id_patient, name, last_name FROM patients WHERE blood_group IS NULL ORDER BY last_name

queries.name: A46 · Patient records with CONCAT
queries.description: Joins name and surname with CONCAT, and the blood group with the city: the first 7 patients by identifier. The result is null when there is no blood group.
queries.sql: SELECT CONCAT(name, ' ', last_name) AS patient, CONCAT(blood_group, ' · ', city) AS blood_city FROM patients ORDER BY id_patient LIMIT 7

queries.name: A47 · Global admission totals with every aggregate (no GROUP BY)
queries.description: Aggregates without GROUP BY over the 50 admissions: 28 patients and 9 different reasons; total 30404, minimum 192, maximum 950 and rounded average 608.08.
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS admissions, COUNT(cost_per_day) AS with_cost, COUNT(DISTINCT id_patient) AS patients, COUNT(DISTINCT reason) AS reasons, SUM(cost_per_day) AS total_cost, MIN(cost_per_day) AS minimum, MAX(cost_per_day) AS maximum, ROUND(AVG(cost_per_day), 2) AS average FROM admissions

queries.name: A48 · Invoices by payment method with COUNT of a column and HAVING (column with NULL)
queries.description: GROUP BY on a column with nulls: COALESCE labels the group without a method and COUNT(payment_method) leaves it at zero; HAVING keeps the groups adding up to 65000 or more.
queries.sql: SELECT COALESCE(payment_method, 'no method') AS method, COUNT(*) AS invoices, COUNT(payment_method) AS with_method, COUNT(DISTINCT id_patient) AS patients, SUM(amount) AS total, ROUND(AVG(amount), 2) AS average FROM invoices GROUP BY payment_method HAVING SUM(amount) >= 65000 ORDER BY total DESC

queries.name: A49 · Appointments by doctor and status (GROUP BY of two columns with HAVING)
queries.description: Two grouping columns with COUNT(*) and MIN and MAX of the duration: only three doctor-status combinations reach 4 appointments.
queries.sql: SELECT id_doctor, status, COUNT(*) AS appointments, MIN(duration_min) AS minimum, MAX(duration_min) AS maximum FROM appointments GROUP BY id_doctor, status HAVING COUNT(*) >= 4 ORDER BY appointments DESC, id_doctor, status

queries.name: A50 · Patients by blood group (COUNT(*) versus COUNT of a column)
queries.description: The unknown group shows up in COUNT(*) but at zero in COUNT(blood_group); COUNT(DISTINCT city) counts different cities per group and the HAVING requires 3 patients.
queries.sql: SELECT COALESCE(blood_group, 'unknown') AS blood_group, COUNT(*) AS patients, COUNT(blood_group) AS with_group, COUNT(DISTINCT city) AS cities FROM patients GROUP BY blood_group HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ORDER BY patients DESC, blood_group

queries.name: A51 · Admissions per doctor with every numeric aggregate (double HAVING)
queries.description: COUNT(*), SUM, MIN, MAX and AVG of the cost per doctor; HAVING combines COUNT(*) and AVG: three admissions at least and an average of 600 or more.
queries.sql: SELECT id_doctor, COUNT(*) AS admissions, SUM(cost_per_day) AS total_cost, MIN(cost_per_day) AS minimum, MAX(cost_per_day) AS maximum, ROUND(AVG(cost_per_day), 2) AS average FROM admissions GROUP BY id_doctor HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 AND AVG(cost_per_day) >= 600 ORDER BY total_cost DESC, id_doctor

queries.name: A52 · Rooms by hospital and occupancy (GROUP BY of two columns with SUM)
queries.description: Grouping by hospital and occupancy with COUNT(*) and SUM(num_beds); HAVING keeps only the groups of 4 rooms or more.
queries.sql: SELECT id_hospital, occupied, COUNT(*) AS rooms, SUM(num_beds) AS beds FROM rooms GROUP BY id_hospital, occupied HAVING COUNT(*) >= 4 ORDER BY id_hospital, occupied

queries.name: A53 · Surgeries by risk with every function (HAVING SUM)
queries.description: COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT operating_room), SUM, MIN, MAX and AVG by risk; the HAVING on the sum leaves out the high risk.
queries.sql: SELECT risk, COUNT(*) AS surgeries, COUNT(DISTINCT operating_room) AS operating_rooms, SUM(cost) AS total_cost, MIN(duration_min) AS min_duration, MAX(duration_min) AS max_duration, ROUND(AVG(cost), 0) AS average_cost FROM surgeries GROUP BY risk HAVING SUM(cost) > 65000 ORDER BY total_cost DESC

queries.name: A54 · Labs by type with COUNT(DISTINCT) and AVG (HAVING COUNT DISTINCT)
queries.description: Per lab type: COUNT(*) of rows, COUNT(DISTINCT id_patient) of patients and two rounded AVGs; HAVING requires 15 different patients.
queries.sql: SELECT type, COUNT(*) AS labs, COUNT(DISTINCT id_patient) AS patients, ROUND(AVG(glucose), 1) AS average_glucose, ROUND(AVG(cholesterol), 1) AS average_cholesterol FROM labs GROUP BY type HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT id_patient) >= 15 ORDER BY labs DESC

queries.name: A55 · Prescriptions per drug with SUM, MIN, MAX and AVG (HAVING COUNT)
queries.description: Per drug, COUNT(*) with SUM of the amounts and MIN, MAX and AVG of the duration; HAVING requires 8 prescriptions or more.
queries.sql: SELECT id_drug, COUNT(*) AS prescriptions, SUM(amount) AS units, MIN(duration_days) AS min_days, MAX(duration_days) AS max_days, ROUND(AVG(duration_days), 1) AS average_days FROM prescriptions GROUP BY id_drug HAVING COUNT(*) >= 8 ORDER BY units DESC, id_drug

queries.name: A56 · Treatments per year with SUM and AVG (GROUP BY with an expression and HAVING)
queries.description: GROUP BY on the year of the start date: COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT id_patient), SUM and rounded AVG of the cost; HAVING keeps the years with 10 treatments or more.
queries.sql: SELECT SUBSTR(start_date, 1, 4) AS year, COUNT(*) AS treatments, COUNT(DISTINCT id_patient) AS patients, SUM(cost) AS total_cost, ROUND(AVG(cost), 0) AS average_cost FROM treatments GROUP BY SUBSTR(start_date, 1, 4) HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10 ORDER BY year

queries.name: A57 · Aggregates over the grouped column itself (COUNT of status)
queries.description: COUNT(status) matches COUNT(*) and COUNT(DISTINCT status) is 1 in every group; MAX(id_appointment) and COUNT(duration_min) summarise the other columns.
queries.sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS total, COUNT(status) AS with_status, COUNT(DISTINCT status) AS statuses, MAX(id_appointment) AS last_id, COUNT(duration_min) AS with_duration FROM appointments GROUP BY status ORDER BY total DESC, status

queries.name: A58 · HAVING with aggregates that are not in the SELECT
queries.description: HAVING with COUNT(*) and MIN(duration_min) outside the SELECT: only the pending appointments have more than 10 appointments and go below 20 minutes.
queries.sql: SELECT status FROM appointments GROUP BY status HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10 AND MIN(duration_min) < 20 ORDER BY status

queries.name: A59 · Emergency admissions by reason (WHERE, GROUP BY and HAVING)
queries.description: WHERE keeps only the emergencies and then groups by reason: COUNT(*) of admissions and COUNT(cost_per_day) of those with a cost, with HAVING of 4 or more.
queries.sql: SELECT reason, COUNT(*) AS admissions, COUNT(cost_per_day) AS with_cost FROM admissions WHERE is_emergency = true GROUP BY reason HAVING COUNT(*) >= 4 ORDER BY admissions DESC, reason

queries.name: B01 · Hospitals with their services
queries.description: INNER JOIN 1:M between hospital and service.
queries.sql: SELECT h.name AS hospital, s.name AS service, s.bed_capacity FROM hospitals AS h INNER JOIN services AS s ON s.id_hospital = h.id_hospital ORDER BY h.name, s.name

queries.name: B02 · Services with their hospital and specialty
queries.description: Three tables chained.
queries.sql: SELECT s.name AS service, e.name AS specialty, h.name AS hospital FROM services AS s INNER JOIN specialties AS e ON e.id_specialty = s.id_specialty INNER JOIN hospitals AS h ON h.id_hospital = s.id_hospital ORDER BY h.name, s.name

queries.name: B03 · Hospitals without services
queries.description: LEFT JOIN to find the orphans.
queries.sql: SELECT h.name AS hospital FROM hospitals AS h LEFT JOIN services AS s ON s.id_hospital = h.id_hospital WHERE s.id_service IS NULL ORDER BY h.name

queries.name: B04 · Specialties without doctors
queries.description: LEFT JOIN and filter by null.
queries.sql: SELECT e.name AS specialty FROM specialties AS e LEFT JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_specialty = e.id_specialty WHERE m.id_doctor IS NULL ORDER BY e.name

queries.name: B05 · Implicit join: doctors and services
queries.description: Relationship with commas in the FROM.
queries.sql: SELECT m.name, m.last_name, s.name AS service FROM doctors AS m, services AS s WHERE m.id_service = s.id_service AND s.id_hospital = 1 ORDER BY m.last_name

queries.name: B06 · Doctors with their specialty
queries.description: INNER JOIN by the specialty key.
queries.sql: SELECT m.last_name, m.name, e.name AS specialty, m.category FROM doctors AS m INNER JOIN specialties AS e ON e.id_specialty = m.id_specialty ORDER BY m.last_name LIMIT 15

queries.name: B07 · Specialties with at least three doctors
queries.description: LEFT JOIN + HAVING.
queries.sql: SELECT e.name AS specialty, COUNT(m.id_doctor) AS doctors FROM specialties AS e LEFT JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_specialty = e.id_specialty GROUP BY e.name HAVING COUNT(m.id_doctor) >= 3 ORDER BY doctors DESC

queries.name: B08 · Patients by insurer
queries.description: Grouping of a join with the coverage.
queries.sql: SELECT s.name AS insurance, COUNT(p.id_patient) AS patients, s.coverage_percent FROM insurers AS s LEFT JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_insurer = s.id_insurer GROUP BY s.name, s.coverage_percent ORDER BY patients DESC

queries.name: B09 · Rooms by hospital
queries.description: LEFT JOIN counting rooms, even when they are 0.
queries.sql: SELECT h.name AS hospital, COUNT(rm.id_room) AS rooms, SUM(rm.num_beds) AS beds FROM hospitals AS h LEFT JOIN rooms AS rm ON rm.id_hospital = h.id_hospital GROUP BY h.name ORDER BY rooms DESC

queries.name: B10 · Admissions with patient, room and doctor
queries.description: Four tables in the same join.
queries.sql: SELECT i.id_admission, p.last_name AS patient, rm.code AS room, m.last_name AS doctor, i.reason FROM admissions AS i INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = i.id_patient LEFT JOIN rooms AS rm ON rm.id_room = i.id_room INNER JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_doctor = i.id_doctor ORDER BY i.id_admission LIMIT 25

queries.name: B11 · Appointments with patient and doctor
queries.description: Join of the schedule.
queries.sql: SELECT c.id_appointment, c.date, p.last_name AS patient, m.last_name AS doctor, c.status FROM appointments AS c INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = c.id_patient INNER JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_doctor = c.id_doctor ORDER BY c.date DESC, c.time LIMIT 25

queries.name: B12 · Visits with their doctor
queries.description: Direct join with order by date.
queries.sql: SELECT v.id_visit, v.date, v.reason, m.last_name AS doctor FROM visits AS v INNER JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_doctor = v.id_doctor ORDER BY v.date, v.id_visit LIMIT 20

queries.name: B13 · Surgeries with patient and surgeon
queries.description: Two joins and a filter by risk.
queries.sql: SELECT iv.name AS surgery, p.last_name AS patient, m.last_name AS surgeon, iv.risk FROM surgeries AS iv INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = iv.id_patient INNER JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_doctor = iv.id_doctor WHERE iv.risk = 'high' ORDER BY iv.cost DESC

queries.name: B14 · Cartesian product specialties × hospitals
queries.description: Without a join condition: every combination.
queries.sql: SELECT h.name AS hospital, e.name AS specialty FROM hospitals AS h, specialties AS e ORDER BY h.id_hospital, e.id_specialty

queries.name: B15 · The five most expensive drugs
queries.description: Join with prescriptions and a limit.
queries.sql: SELECT med.name, med.price, COUNT(*) AS prescriptions FROM drugs AS med INNER JOIN prescriptions AS pr ON pr.id_drug = med.id_drug GROUP BY med.name, med.price ORDER BY med.price DESC LIMIT 5

queries.name: B16 · Specialties with distinct doctors
queries.description: COUNT DISTINCT inside a join.
queries.sql: SELECT e.name AS specialty, COUNT(DISTINCT m.id_doctor) AS doctors, COUNT(DISTINCT s.id_service) AS services FROM specialties AS e LEFT JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_specialty = e.id_specialty LEFT JOIN services AS s ON s.id_specialty = e.id_specialty GROUP BY e.name ORDER BY doctors DESC

queries.name: B17 · Experience by category
queries.description: MIN and MAX per group.
queries.sql: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS doctors, MIN(years_experience) AS min_experience, MAX(years_experience) AS max_experience FROM doctors GROUP BY category ORDER BY max_experience DESC

queries.name: B18 · Active treatments with patient and diagnosis
queries.description: Join of three tables and a boolean filter.
queries.sql: SELECT t.id_treatment, p.last_name AS patient, d.name AS diagnosis, t.cost FROM treatments AS t INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = t.id_patient INNER JOIN diagnoses AS d ON d.id_diagnosis = t.id_diagnosis WHERE t.active = true ORDER BY t.cost DESC LIMIT 20

queries.name: B19 · Abnormal lab tests with patient and doctor
queries.description: Boolean filter on a join.
queries.sql: SELECT a.id_lab, p.last_name AS patient, m.last_name AS doctor, a.glucose, a.cholesterol FROM labs AS a INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = a.id_patient INNER JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_doctor = a.id_doctor WHERE a.is_abnormal = true ORDER BY a.date DESC LIMIT 20

queries.name: B20 · Unpaid invoices with their patient
queries.description: LEFT JOIN of the insurer and a boolean filter.
queries.sql: SELECT f.id_invoice, p.last_name AS patient, f.amount, s.name AS insurance FROM invoices AS f INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = f.id_patient LEFT JOIN insurers AS s ON s.id_insurer = p.id_insurer WHERE f.paid = false ORDER BY f.amount DESC LIMIT 20

queries.name: B21 · Active admissions with their room
queries.description: IS NULL for the ones still admitted.
queries.sql: SELECT i.id_admission, p.last_name AS patient, rm.code, i.admission_date FROM admissions AS i INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = i.id_patient LEFT JOIN rooms AS rm ON rm.id_room = i.id_room WHERE i.discharge_date IS NULL ORDER BY i.admission_date

queries.name: B22 · Nurses and their service
queries.description: Join with data of both.
queries.sql: SELECT nur.last_name AS nurse, nur.shift, s.name AS service, h.name AS hospital FROM nurses AS nur INNER JOIN services AS s ON s.id_service = nur.id_service INNER JOIN hospitals AS h ON h.id_hospital = s.id_hospital ORDER BY nur.last_name LIMIT 20

queries.name: B23 · Visits with their main diagnosis
queries.description: Join visit → relationship → diagnosis.
queries.sql: SELECT v.id_visit, v.reason, d.name AS diagnosis, d.severity FROM visits AS v INNER JOIN visit_diagnoses AS vd ON vd.id_visit = v.id_visit INNER JOIN diagnoses AS d ON d.id_diagnosis = vd.id_diagnosis WHERE vd.is_main = true ORDER BY v.id_visit LIMIT 25

queries.name: B24 · Prescriptions with drug and treatment
queries.description: Resolves the M:N showing both ends.
queries.sql: SELECT pr.id_prescription, med.name AS drug, pr.dose, t.id_treatment, p.last_name AS patient FROM prescriptions AS pr INNER JOIN drugs AS med ON med.id_drug = pr.id_drug INNER JOIN treatments AS t ON t.id_treatment = pr.id_treatment INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = t.id_patient ORDER BY pr.id_prescription LIMIT 25

queries.name: B25 · Treatments by diagnosis
queries.description: GROUP BY of a join with HAVING.
queries.sql: SELECT d.name AS diagnosis, COUNT(t.id_treatment) AS treatments, ROUND(AVG(t.cost), 0) AS avg_cost FROM diagnoses AS d INNER JOIN treatments AS t ON t.id_diagnosis = d.id_diagnosis GROUP BY d.name HAVING COUNT(t.id_treatment) >= 2 ORDER BY treatments DESC

queries.name: B26 · Cost of treatments by doctor
queries.description: SUM and COUNT grouped.
queries.sql: SELECT m.last_name AS doctor, COUNT(*) AS treatments, SUM(t.cost) AS total_cost FROM treatments AS t INNER JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_doctor = t.id_doctor GROUP BY m.last_name ORDER BY total_cost DESC LIMIT 10

queries.name: B27 · Surgeries by risk level
queries.description: Grouping with the average cost.
queries.sql: SELECT risk, COUNT(*) AS surgeries, ROUND(AVG(cost), 0) AS avg_cost FROM surgeries GROUP BY risk ORDER BY avg_cost DESC

queries.name: B28 · Patients with insurer and city
queries.description: Join with COALESCE for the missing insurer.
queries.sql: SELECT p.last_name AS patient, COALESCE(s.name, 'no insurer') AS insurance, p.city FROM patients AS p LEFT JOIN insurers AS s ON s.id_insurer = p.id_insurer ORDER BY p.city, p.last_name LIMIT 25

queries.name: B29 · Allergies with the drug involved
queries.description: LEFT JOIN because there are allergies without a drug.
queries.sql: SELECT alg.substance, alg.severity, med.name AS drug, p.last_name AS patient FROM allergies AS alg LEFT JOIN drugs AS med ON med.id_drug = alg.id_drug INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = alg.id_patient ORDER BY alg.severity DESC, alg.substance LIMIT 25

queries.name: B30 · Beds by hospital (only those with rooms)
queries.description: INNER JOIN and sum of beds.
queries.sql: SELECT h.name AS hospital, COUNT(rm.id_room) AS rooms, SUM(rm.num_beds) AS beds FROM hospitals AS h INNER JOIN rooms AS rm ON rm.id_hospital = h.id_hospital GROUP BY h.name ORDER BY beds DESC

queries.name: B31 · Admissions by month
queries.description: GROUP BY with SUBSTR on the date.
queries.sql: SELECT SUBSTR(admission_date, 1, 7) AS month, COUNT(*) AS admissions FROM admissions GROUP BY SUBSTR(admission_date, 1, 7) ORDER BY month

queries.name: B32 · Billing by year
queries.description: SUBSTR for the year and sum of amounts.
queries.sql: SELECT SUBSTR(date, 1, 4) AS year, COUNT(*) AS invoices, SUM(amount) AS total FROM invoices GROUP BY SUBSTR(date, 1, 4) ORDER BY year

queries.name: B33 · Doctors with more visits
queries.description: Join and GROUP BY with LIMIT.
queries.sql: SELECT m.last_name AS doctor, COUNT(v.id_visit) AS visits FROM doctors AS m INNER JOIN visits AS v ON v.id_doctor = m.id_doctor GROUP BY m.last_name ORDER BY visits DESC LIMIT 10

queries.name: B34 · Cancelled appointments by doctor
queries.description: Status filter on a join.
queries.sql: SELECT m.last_name AS doctor, COUNT(*) AS cancelled FROM appointments AS c INNER JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_doctor = c.id_doctor WHERE c.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY m.last_name ORDER BY cancelled DESC LIMIT 10

queries.name: B35 · Diagnoses by specialty
queries.description: COUNT on a join.
queries.sql: SELECT e.name AS specialty, COUNT(d.id_diagnosis) AS diagnoses FROM specialties AS e LEFT JOIN diagnoses AS d ON d.id_specialty = e.id_specialty GROUP BY e.name ORDER BY diagnoses DESC

queries.name: B36 · Drugs by treatment
queries.description: Counts the M:N with ORDER BY of an aggregate.
queries.sql: SELECT t.id_treatment, p.last_name AS patient, COUNT(pr.id_prescription) AS drugs FROM treatments AS t INNER JOIN prescriptions AS pr ON pr.id_treatment = t.id_treatment INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = t.id_patient GROUP BY t.id_treatment, p.last_name ORDER BY drugs DESC, t.id_treatment LIMIT 15

queries.name: B37 · Surgeries by operating room
queries.description: Grouping with a count and extreme durations.
queries.sql: SELECT operating_room, COUNT(*) AS surgeries, MIN(duration_min) AS min_duration, MAX(duration_min) AS max_duration FROM surgeries GROUP BY operating_room ORDER BY surgeries DESC

queries.name: B38 · Chronic patients with active treatments
queries.description: Two filters and a join of three tables.
queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.last_name AS patient, p.city FROM patients AS p INNER JOIN treatments AS t ON t.id_patient = p.id_patient WHERE p.is_chronic = true AND t.active = true ORDER BY p.last_name

queries.name: B39 · Specialties with more visits
queries.description: Chain service → specialty → visits.
queries.sql: SELECT e.name AS specialty, COUNT(v.id_visit) AS visits FROM visits AS v INNER JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_doctor = v.id_doctor INNER JOIN specialties AS e ON e.id_specialty = m.id_specialty GROUP BY e.name ORDER BY visits DESC

queries.name: B40 · Visits by appointment type
queries.description: LEFT JOIN to include the walk-ins.
queries.sql: SELECT COALESCE(c.type, 'walk-in') AS type, COUNT(v.id_visit) AS visits FROM visits AS v LEFT JOIN appointments AS c ON c.id_appointment = v.id_appointment GROUP BY c.type ORDER BY visits DESC

queries.name: B41 · Occupied and free rooms by hospital
queries.description: GROUP BY of two columns, the boolean state included.
queries.sql: SELECT h.name AS hospital, rm.occupied, COUNT(*) AS rooms FROM hospitals AS h INNER JOIN rooms AS rm ON rm.id_hospital = h.id_hospital GROUP BY h.name, rm.occupied ORDER BY h.name, rm.occupied

queries.name: B42 · Emergency admissions by hospital
queries.description: Join patient, admission and hospital.
queries.sql: SELECT h.name AS hospital, COUNT(*) AS urgent FROM admissions AS i INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = i.id_patient INNER JOIN rooms AS rm ON rm.id_room = i.id_room INNER JOIN hospitals AS h ON h.id_hospital = rm.id_hospital WHERE i.is_emergency = true GROUP BY h.name ORDER BY urgent DESC

queries.name: B43 · Average coverage of invoices by insurer
queries.description: Join and grouped average.
queries.sql: SELECT s.name AS insurance, COUNT(f.id_invoice) AS invoices, ROUND(AVG(f.amount), 0) AS avg_amount FROM invoices AS f INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = f.id_patient INNER JOIN insurers AS s ON s.id_insurer = p.id_insurer GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY avg_amount DESC

queries.name: B44 · Lab tests by type and result
queries.description: GROUP BY of two columns.
queries.sql: SELECT type, is_abnormal, COUNT(*) AS labs FROM labs GROUP BY type, is_abnormal ORDER BY type, is_abnormal

queries.name: B45 · Severe diagnoses with treatments
queries.description: Join and filter by severity.
queries.sql: SELECT d.name AS diagnosis, d.severity, COUNT(t.id_treatment) AS treatments FROM diagnoses AS d INNER JOIN treatments AS t ON t.id_diagnosis = d.id_diagnosis WHERE d.severity = 'severe' GROUP BY d.name, d.severity ORDER BY treatments DESC

queries.name: C01 · History of one patient
queries.description: Gathers admissions, appointments and visits of one patient with distinct counts.
queries.sql: SELECT p.last_name AS patient, COUNT(DISTINCT i.id_admission) AS admissions, COUNT(DISTINCT c.id_appointment) AS appointments, COUNT(DISTINCT v.id_visit) AS visits FROM patients AS p LEFT JOIN admissions AS i ON i.id_patient = p.id_patient LEFT JOIN appointments AS c ON c.id_patient = p.id_patient LEFT JOIN visits AS v ON v.id_patient = p.id_patient WHERE p.id_patient = 1 GROUP BY p.last_name

queries.name: C02 · Visits with two or more diagnoses
queries.description: GROUP BY on the M:N link with HAVING.
queries.sql: SELECT v.id_visit, v.reason, COUNT(vd.id_diagnosis) AS diagnoses FROM visits AS v INNER JOIN visit_diagnoses AS vd ON vd.id_visit = v.id_visit GROUP BY v.id_visit, v.reason HAVING COUNT(vd.id_diagnosis) >= 2 ORDER BY diagnoses DESC, v.id_visit LIMIT 20

queries.name: C03 · Most frequent diagnoses
queries.description: Counts appearances in the bridge table.
queries.sql: SELECT d.name AS diagnosis, COUNT(*) AS times FROM visit_diagnoses AS vd INNER JOIN diagnoses AS d ON d.id_diagnosis = vd.id_diagnosis GROUP BY d.name ORDER BY times DESC, diagnosis LIMIT 10

queries.name: C04 · Treatments with more than two drugs
queries.description: HAVING on the M:N of prescriptions.
queries.sql: SELECT t.id_treatment, COUNT(pr.id_drug) AS drugs FROM treatments AS t INNER JOIN prescriptions AS pr ON pr.id_treatment = t.id_treatment GROUP BY t.id_treatment HAVING COUNT(pr.id_drug) > 2 ORDER BY drugs DESC LIMIT 15

queries.name: C05 · Most prescribed drugs
queries.description: Ranking from the bridge table.
queries.sql: SELECT med.name AS drug, COUNT(*) AS prescriptions FROM prescriptions AS pr INNER JOIN drugs AS med ON med.id_drug = pr.id_drug GROUP BY med.name ORDER BY prescriptions DESC, drug LIMIT 10

queries.name: C06 · Patients with more invoices
queries.description: JOIN and ORDER BY of an aggregate with LIMIT.
queries.sql: SELECT p.last_name AS patient, COUNT(f.id_invoice) AS invoices, SUM(f.amount) AS total FROM patients AS p INNER JOIN invoices AS f ON f.id_patient = p.id_patient GROUP BY p.last_name ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 10

queries.name: C07 · Patients who never had an appointment
queries.description: LEFT JOIN and check for null.
queries.sql: SELECT p.last_name AS patient FROM patients AS p LEFT JOIN appointments AS c ON c.id_patient = p.id_patient WHERE c.id_appointment IS NULL ORDER BY p.last_name

queries.name: C08 · Doctors without any appointment
queries.description: Those on the staff who never appear in the schedule.
queries.sql: SELECT m.last_name AS doctor FROM doctors AS m LEFT JOIN appointments AS c ON c.id_doctor = m.id_doctor WHERE c.id_appointment IS NULL ORDER BY m.last_name

queries.name: C09 · Rooms without admissions
queries.description: LEFT JOIN from the rooms.
queries.sql: SELECT rm.code, rm.type FROM rooms AS rm LEFT JOIN admissions AS i ON i.id_room = rm.id_room WHERE i.id_admission IS NULL ORDER BY rm.code

queries.name: C10 · Nobody has two insurers (rowCount)
queries.description: Integrity check: the result must be empty.
queries.sql: SELECT id_patient, COUNT(DISTINCT id_insurer) AS insurers FROM patients WHERE id_insurer IS NOT NULL GROUP BY id_patient HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT id_insurer) >= 2

queries.name: C11 · Patients without lab tests
queries.description: LEFT JOIN on the laboratory.
queries.sql: SELECT p.last_name AS patient FROM patients AS p LEFT JOIN labs AS a ON a.id_patient = p.id_patient WHERE a.id_lab IS NULL ORDER BY p.last_name

queries.name: C12 · Visits of one patient regardless of the order
queries.description: Assert with ignoreOrder: the set is compared.
queries.sql: SELECT v.reason FROM visits AS v WHERE v.id_patient = 5

queries.name: C13 · Specialty with more admissions
queries.description: Chain admission → doctor → specialty.
queries.sql: SELECT e.name AS specialty, COUNT(*) AS admissions FROM admissions AS i INNER JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_doctor = i.id_doctor INNER JOIN specialties AS e ON e.id_specialty = m.id_specialty GROUP BY e.name ORDER BY admissions DESC LIMIT 5

queries.name: C14 · Drugs with more allergies
queries.description: Bridge table allergies-drug.
queries.sql: SELECT med.name AS drug, COUNT(*) AS allergies FROM allergies AS alg INNER JOIN drugs AS med ON med.id_drug = alg.id_drug GROUP BY med.name ORDER BY allergies DESC, drug LIMIT 10

queries.name: C15 · Diagnoses without treatments
queries.description: LEFT JOIN from the catalogue.
queries.sql: SELECT d.name AS diagnosis FROM diagnoses AS d LEFT JOIN treatments AS t ON t.id_diagnosis = d.id_diagnosis WHERE t.id_treatment IS NULL ORDER BY d.name

queries.name: C16 · Doctors with more surgeries
queries.description: Ranking of surgeons.
queries.sql: SELECT m.last_name AS doctor, COUNT(*) AS surgeries, SUM(iv.cost) AS total_cost FROM surgeries AS iv INNER JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_doctor = iv.id_doctor GROUP BY m.last_name ORDER BY surgeries DESC, total_cost DESC LIMIT 10

queries.name: C17 · Treatments without prescriptions
queries.description: LEFT JOIN on the M:N.
queries.sql: SELECT t.id_treatment FROM treatments AS t LEFT JOIN prescriptions AS pr ON pr.id_treatment = t.id_treatment WHERE pr.id_prescription IS NULL ORDER BY t.id_treatment

queries.name: C18 · Prescriptions of one treatment
queries.description: Concrete filter on the bridge table.
queries.sql: SELECT med.name AS drug, pr.dose, pr.duration_days FROM prescriptions AS pr INNER JOIN drugs AS med ON med.id_drug = pr.id_drug WHERE pr.id_treatment = 4 ORDER BY med.name

queries.name: C19 · Insurers with their patients
queries.description: LEFT JOIN to include insurers without patients.
queries.sql: SELECT s.name AS insurance, COUNT(p.id_patient) AS patients FROM insurers AS s LEFT JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_insurer = s.id_insurer GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY patients DESC

queries.name: C20 · Nursing supervisors by service
queries.description: Boolean filter and join.
queries.sql: SELECT s.name AS service, COUNT(*) AS supervisors FROM nurses AS nur INNER JOIN services AS s ON s.id_service = nur.id_service WHERE nur.is_supervisor = true GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY supervisors DESC

queries.name: C21 · Patients with more than five visits
queries.description: Count on the visits with HAVING.
queries.sql: SELECT p.last_name AS patient, COUNT(*) AS visits FROM visits AS v INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = v.id_patient GROUP BY p.last_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 ORDER BY visits DESC

queries.name: C22 · Hospitals with more admissions
queries.description: Chain hospital → room → admission.
queries.sql: SELECT h.name AS hospital, COUNT(*) AS admissions FROM admissions AS i INNER JOIN rooms AS rm ON rm.id_room = i.id_room INNER JOIN hospitals AS h ON h.id_hospital = rm.id_hospital GROUP BY h.name ORDER BY admissions DESC

queries.name: C23 · Specialties with more doctors
queries.description: Ranking of staffing.
queries.sql: SELECT e.name AS specialty, COUNT(*) AS doctors FROM doctors AS m INNER JOIN specialties AS e ON e.id_specialty = m.id_specialty GROUP BY e.name ORDER BY doctors DESC, specialty

queries.name: C24 · Invoices that go over 75% of the coverage
queries.description: Compares the amount with a calculation on the insurer.
queries.sql: SELECT f.id_invoice, f.amount, s.coverage_percent FROM invoices AS f INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = f.id_patient INNER JOIN insurers AS s ON s.id_insurer = p.id_insurer WHERE f.amount * s.coverage_percent / 100 > 3000 ORDER BY f.amount DESC LIMIT 20

queries.name: C25 · Appointments of one specific day
queries.description: Exact date filter with a join (a date that exists in the data).
queries.sql: SELECT c.time, p.last_name AS patient, m.last_name AS doctor, c.status FROM appointments AS c INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = c.id_patient INNER JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_doctor = c.id_doctor WHERE c.date = '2024-02-16' ORDER BY c.time

queries.name: C26 · Surgeries without a linked admission
queries.description: IS NULL filter on the foreign key.
queries.sql: SELECT iv.name, iv.date, iv.cost FROM surgeries AS iv WHERE iv.id_admission IS NULL ORDER BY iv.date DESC

queries.name: C27 · Patients allergic to a drug they take
queries.description: Crosses allergies and prescriptions of the same patient.
queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.last_name AS patient, med.name AS drug FROM allergies AS alg INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = alg.id_patient INNER JOIN drugs AS med ON med.id_drug = alg.id_drug INNER JOIN treatments AS t ON t.id_patient = p.id_patient INNER JOIN prescriptions AS pr ON pr.id_treatment = t.id_treatment AND pr.id_drug = med.id_drug ORDER BY p.last_name, med.name

queries.name: C28 · Admissions by the specialty of the doctor
queries.description: Groups by the specialty of the doctor in charge.
queries.sql: SELECT e.name AS specialty, COUNT(*) AS admissions, ROUND(AVG(i.cost_per_day), 0) AS avg_cost FROM admissions AS i INNER JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_doctor = i.id_doctor INNER JOIN specialties AS e ON e.id_specialty = m.id_specialty GROUP BY e.name ORDER BY admissions DESC

queries.name: C29 · Billing by insurer type
queries.description: SUM and COUNT grouped by the type.
queries.sql: SELECT s.type, COUNT(f.id_invoice) AS invoices, SUM(f.amount) AS total FROM invoices AS f INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = f.id_patient INNER JOIN insurers AS s ON s.id_insurer = p.id_insurer GROUP BY s.type ORDER BY total DESC

queries.name: C30 · Most frequent main diagnosis by severity
queries.description: Filter of main and GROUP BY of severity.
queries.sql: SELECT d.severity, d.name AS diagnosis, COUNT(*) AS times FROM visit_diagnoses AS vd INNER JOIN diagnoses AS d ON d.id_diagnosis = vd.id_diagnosis WHERE vd.is_main = true GROUP BY d.severity, d.name ORDER BY times DESC LIMIT 10

queries.name: C31 · Patients with more than one distinct diagnosis
queries.description: COUNT DISTINCT on the M:N.
queries.sql: SELECT p.last_name AS patient, COUNT(DISTINCT d.id_diagnosis) AS diagnoses FROM patients AS p INNER JOIN visits AS v ON v.id_patient = p.id_patient INNER JOIN visit_diagnoses AS vd ON vd.id_visit = v.id_visit INNER JOIN diagnoses AS d ON d.id_diagnosis = vd.id_diagnosis GROUP BY p.last_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT d.id_diagnosis) >= 4 ORDER BY diagnoses DESC LIMIT 15

queries.name: C32 · Hospitals with abnormal lab tests
queries.description: Chain hospital → service → doctor → lab test.
queries.sql: SELECT h.name AS hospital, COUNT(*) AS abnormal FROM labs AS a INNER JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_doctor = a.id_doctor INNER JOIN services AS s ON s.id_service = m.id_service INNER JOIN hospitals AS h ON h.id_hospital = s.id_hospital WHERE a.is_abnormal = true GROUP BY h.name ORDER BY abnormal DESC

queries.name: C33 · Average cost by type of visit
queries.description: Groups the visits with and without follow-up.
queries.sql: SELECT needs_follow_up, COUNT(*) AS visits, ROUND(AVG(cost), 2) AS avg_cost FROM visits GROUP BY needs_follow_up ORDER BY avg_cost DESC

queries.name: C34 · Total stock by route of administration
queries.description: SUM and COUNT grouped.
queries.sql: SELECT route, COUNT(*) AS drugs, SUM(stock) AS total_stock FROM drugs GROUP BY route ORDER BY total_stock DESC

queries.name: C35 · Ranking of patients by spending on treatments
queries.description: SUM grouped with HAVING and LIMIT.
queries.sql: SELECT p.last_name AS patient, SUM(t.cost) AS spending FROM treatments AS t INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = t.id_patient GROUP BY p.last_name HAVING SUM(t.cost) > 2000 ORDER BY spending DESC LIMIT 10

queries.name: D01 · Admissions without a patient
queries.description: Broken foreign key: the row in patients is not found.
queries.sql: SELECT i.id_admission, i.id_patient FROM admissions AS i LEFT JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = i.id_patient WHERE p.id_patient IS NULL ORDER BY i.id_admission

queries.name: D02 · Admissions without a doctor
queries.description: The doctor key finds no row.
queries.sql: SELECT i.id_admission, i.id_doctor FROM admissions AS i LEFT JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_doctor = i.id_doctor WHERE m.id_doctor IS NULL ORDER BY i.id_admission

queries.name: D03 · Appointments without a patient
queries.description: Broken reference in the schedule.
queries.sql: SELECT c.id_appointment, c.id_patient FROM appointments AS c LEFT JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = c.id_patient WHERE p.id_patient IS NULL ORDER BY c.id_appointment

queries.name: D04 · Appointments without a doctor
queries.description: Broken reference to the physician.
queries.sql: SELECT c.id_appointment, c.id_doctor FROM appointments AS c LEFT JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id_doctor = c.id_doctor WHERE m.id_doctor IS NULL ORDER BY c.id_appointment

queries.name: D05 · Patients with an insurer that does not exist
queries.description: The key points at an insurer that is not there.
queries.sql: SELECT p.id_patient, p.id_insurer FROM patients AS p LEFT JOIN insurers AS s ON s.id_insurer = p.id_insurer WHERE p.id_insurer IS NOT NULL AND s.id_insurer IS NULL ORDER BY p.id_patient

queries.name: D06 · Prescriptions without a drug
queries.description: Orphan prescription line.
queries.sql: SELECT pr.id_prescription, pr.id_drug FROM prescriptions AS pr LEFT JOIN drugs AS med ON med.id_drug = pr.id_drug WHERE med.id_drug IS NULL ORDER BY pr.id_prescription

queries.name: D07 · Treatments without a patient
queries.description: Broken reference to the patient.
queries.sql: SELECT t.id_treatment, t.id_patient FROM treatments AS t LEFT JOIN patients AS p ON p.id_patient = t.id_patient WHERE p.id_patient IS NULL ORDER BY t.id_treatment

queries.name: D08 · Walk-in visits without an appointment
queries.description: It is not an error: these visits do not come from the schedule.
queries.sql: SELECT v.id_visit, v.date, v.reason FROM visits AS v WHERE v.id_appointment IS NULL ORDER BY v.id_visit

queries.name: D09 · Patients without an insurer
queries.description: Optional data that is missing.
queries.sql: SELECT id_patient, name, last_name FROM patients WHERE id_insurer IS NULL ORDER BY id_patient

queries.name: D10 · Diagnoses without a specialty
queries.description: Incomplete catalogue.
queries.sql: SELECT d.id_diagnosis, d.name FROM diagnoses AS d LEFT JOIN specialties AS e ON e.id_specialty = d.id_specialty WHERE e.id_specialty IS NULL ORDER BY d.id_diagnosis

queries.name: D11 · Paid invoices without a payment method
queries.description: Inconsistency: charged but with no way of paying.
queries.sql: SELECT id_invoice, amount, paid, payment_method FROM invoices WHERE paid = true AND payment_method IS NULL ORDER BY id_invoice

queries.name: D12 · Unpaid invoices with a payment method
queries.description: The inconsistency symmetrical to the previous one.
queries.sql: SELECT id_invoice, amount, paid, payment_method FROM invoices WHERE paid = false AND payment_method IS NOT NULL ORDER BY id_invoice

queries.name: D13 · Orphan visit-diagnosis relationships
queries.description: The bridge table mentions a visit that does not exist.
queries.sql: SELECT vd.id_vd, vd.id_visit FROM visit_diagnoses AS vd LEFT JOIN visits AS v ON v.id_visit = vd.id_visit WHERE v.id_visit IS NULL ORDER BY vd.id_vd

queries.name: D14 · Rooms without beds
queries.description: A room registered with a capacity of zero.
queries.sql: SELECT id_room, code, type, num_beds FROM rooms WHERE num_beds <= 0 ORDER BY code

queries.name: D15 · Attended appointments without a registered visit
queries.description: The status says attended but there is no visit.
queries.sql: SELECT c.id_appointment, c.date FROM appointments AS c LEFT JOIN visits AS v ON v.id_appointment = c.id_appointment WHERE c.status = 'attended' AND v.id_visit IS NULL ORDER BY c.id_appointment

queries.name: D16 · Secondary diagnoses marked as main
queries.description: There can only be one main diagnosis per visit.
queries.sql: SELECT vd.id_visit, COUNT(*) AS main FROM visit_diagnoses AS vd WHERE vd.is_main = true GROUP BY vd.id_visit HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY vd.id_visit

queries.name: D17 · Surgeries without a previous admission
queries.description: Operated on without any recorded stay.
queries.sql: SELECT id_surgery, name, date FROM surgeries WHERE id_admission IS NULL ORDER BY id_surgery

queries.name: D18 · Treatment costs that are null or negative
queries.description: Values out of range.
queries.sql: SELECT id_treatment, cost FROM treatments WHERE cost IS NULL OR cost < 0 ORDER BY id_treatment

queries.name: D19 · Surgery duration out of range
queries.description: More than five hours is suspicious.
queries.sql: SELECT id_surgery, name, duration_min FROM surgeries WHERE duration_min > 300 ORDER BY duration_min DESC

queries.name: D20 · Prescriptions with a suspicious dose
queries.description: Frequency and duration outside the reasonable ranges.
queries.sql: SELECT id_prescription, dose, frequency_hours, duration_days FROM prescriptions WHERE frequency_hours <= 0 OR duration_days > 90 ORDER BY id_prescription

queries.name: E01 · Simple view: SELECT * of another query
queries.description: The result of A03 is read as a table: the 3 large hospitals with their three columns (name, num_beds, level).
queries.sql: SELECT * FROM [A03 · Large hospitals (>= 800 beds)] ORDER BY num_beds DESC, name

queries.name: E02 · Arithmetic on the columns of a view
queries.description: num_beds is still a number after going through the view A03: it can be divided by 100 and its remainder calculated.
queries.sql: SELECT name AS hospital, num_beds, num_beds / 100 AS hundreds, num_beds % 100 AS remainder FROM [A03 · Large hospitals (>= 800 beds)] ORDER BY num_beds DESC, name

queries.name: E03 · WHERE and DISTINCT on a view
queries.description: Filters the view A03 by num_beds >= 900 and keeps the distinct levels: the three large hospitals are level 4.
queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT level FROM [A03 · Large hospitals (>= 800 beds)] WHERE num_beds >= 900 ORDER BY level

queries.name: E04 · Aggregates on a view
queries.description: Five aggregates in a single row on the result of A03: 3 hospitals, 3450 beds, from 900 to 1350 and an average of 1150.
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS hospitals, SUM(num_beds) AS beds, MIN(num_beds) AS min, MAX(num_beds) AS max, ROUND(AVG(num_beds), 2) AS avg FROM [A03 · Large hospitals (>= 800 beds)]

queries.name: E05 · Levels with two or more large hospitals
queries.description: Groups the view A03 by level and keeps the levels with two or more hospitals: only level 4, with three of them.
queries.sql: SELECT level, COUNT(*) AS hospitals, SUM(num_beds) AS beds FROM [A03 · Large hospitals (>= 800 beds)] GROUP BY level HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY level

queries.name: E06 · A view joined to a base table (INNER JOIN)
queries.description: The view B07 joined to the table specialties by name: the 5 specialties with three or more doctors, with their area and whether they need an ICU.
queries.sql: SELECT b.specialty, b.doctors, e.area, e.needs_icu FROM [B07 · Specialties with at least three doctors] AS b INNER JOIN specialties AS e ON e.name = b.specialty ORDER BY b.doctors DESC, b.specialty

queries.name: E07 · Two views joined by specialty
queries.description: The views C13 and C23 joined by specialty: the 5 specialties of the admissions top that also appear in the ranking of doctors.
queries.sql: SELECT c.specialty, c.admissions, m.doctors FROM [C13 · Specialty with more admissions] AS c INNER JOIN [C23 · Specialties with more doctors] AS m ON m.specialty = c.specialty ORDER BY c.admissions DESC, c.specialty

queries.name: E08 · Table LEFT JOIN view with IS NULL
queries.description: LEFT JOIN of the table hospitals against the view B30 plus IS NULL: the only hospital without rooms, San José Hospital.
queries.sql: SELECT h.name AS hospital FROM hospitals AS h LEFT JOIN [B30 · Beds by hospital (only those with rooms)] AS b ON b.hospital = h.name WHERE b.beds IS NULL ORDER BY h.name

queries.name: E09 · View of a view (two levels of query)
queries.description: Reads the view E05, which in turn reads the view A03: three levels of query chained and a single row (level 4, 3450 beds).
queries.sql: SELECT level, hospitals, beds FROM [E05 · Levels with two or more large hospitals] WHERE beds >= 2000 ORDER BY beds DESC

queries.name: E10 · The same view twice (self join)
queries.description: The view C05 appears twice with different aliases and is joined with itself by the number of prescriptions: the 7 pairs of drugs that share it.
queries.sql: SELECT a.drug AS one, b.drug AS other, a.prescriptions FROM [C05 · Most prescribed drugs] AS a INNER JOIN [C05 · Most prescribed drugs] AS b ON b.prescriptions = a.prescriptions AND b.drug > a.drug ORDER BY a.prescriptions DESC, a.drug, b.drug

queries.name: E11 · Implicit join with commas and a view
queries.description: Cartesian product of the view C19 with the table insurers, filtered by coverage >= 80: the 2 insurers with the highest coverage.
queries.sql: SELECT s.name AS insurance, s.coverage_percent, c.patients FROM [C19 · Insurers with their patients] AS c, insurers AS s WHERE s.name = c.insurance AND s.coverage_percent >= 80 ORDER BY c.patients DESC, s.name

queries.name: E12 · ORDER BY an alias and LIMIT on a view
queries.description: Orders by the alias coverage and cuts the view C19 to 3 rows: the three insurers with more patients.
queries.sql: SELECT insurance AS coverage, patients FROM [C19 · Insurers with their patients] ORDER BY patients DESC, insurance LIMIT 3

queries.name: E13 · A boolean through a view
queries.description: The boolean is_abnormal travels untouched from the table labs to the view B44: only the types urine and blood switch it on.
queries.sql: SELECT type, is_abnormal, labs FROM [B44 · Lab tests by type and result] WHERE is_abnormal = true ORDER BY type

queries.name: E14 · Nulls through a view (COALESCE)
queries.description: The missing phone of «Andes Health» is still null after reading the view A27, and COALESCE replaces it with «no phone».
queries.sql: SELECT name AS insurance, COALESCE(phone, 'no phone') AS contact FROM [A27 · Normalised insurer phone] ORDER BY name

queries.name: E15 · Aggregates on a view that is already aggregated
queries.description: Summarises the already aggregated view B08 (one row per insurer): 6 insurers, 35 patients and between 2 and 9 per insurer.
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS insurers, SUM(patients) AS patients, MIN(patients) AS min, MAX(patients) AS max FROM [B08 · Patients by insurer]

queries.name: E16 · A view that reads a query with LIMIT
queries.description: The view C05 has LIMIT 10: reading it as a table brings only those 10 rows (72 prescriptions in total).
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS drugs, SUM(prescriptions) AS prescriptions FROM [C05 · Most prescribed drugs]

queries.name: E17 · View of an empty result
queries.description: The view C10 returns no rows: reading it as a table gives an empty table, and COUNT(*) returns 0 instead of an error.
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows FROM [C10 · Nobody has two insurers (rowCount)]

queries.name: E18 · LIMIT and OFFSET on a view
queries.description: LIMIT 3 OFFSET 2 on the 8 rows of the view A41: the fourth, fifth and sixth diagnoses by length of the name.
queries.sql: SELECT code, name, letters FROM [A41 · Longest diagnosis names] ORDER BY letters DESC, code LIMIT 3 OFFSET 2

queries.name: E19 · LIKE filter on a view
queries.description: LIKE on a column of the view A37: the 2 drugs with low stock whose name starts with A.
queries.sql: SELECT name, stock, price FROM [A37 · Drugs with low stock] WHERE name LIKE 'A%' ORDER BY name

queries.name: E20 · A view of a view that joins two views
queries.description: Reads the view E07 (which joins C13 and C23) and keeps the specialties with three doctors or more: 4 rows.
queries.sql: SELECT specialty, admissions, doctors FROM [E07 · Two views joined by specialty] WHERE doctors >= 3 ORDER BY doctors DESC, specialty

queries.name: E21 · LEFT JOIN between two views
queries.description: C13 LEFT JOIN C23: the 5 specialties of the admissions top with the number of doctors of each one, from the lowest to the highest.
queries.sql: SELECT c.specialty, c.admissions, m.doctors FROM [C13 · Specialty with more admissions] AS c LEFT JOIN [C23 · Specialties with more doctors] AS m ON m.specialty = c.specialty ORDER BY m.doctors ASC NULLS FIRST, c.specialty

queries.name: E22 · Projection with an alias and a star on a view
queries.description: The star of the alias (v.*) on the view A37: the 6 drugs with low stock, from the lowest to the highest stock.
queries.sql: SELECT v.* FROM [A37 · Drugs with low stock] AS v ORDER BY v.stock

queries.name: E23 · A view that reads a query with several tables
queries.description: The view B10 joins four tables inside (admissions, patients, rooms and doctors): reading it as a table brings its 25 rows.
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows FROM [B10 · Admissions with patient, room and doctor]

queries.name: E24 · Group by a boolean of a view
queries.description: GROUP BY on the boolean needs_follow_up that comes from the view C33: the visits with and without follow-up.
queries.sql: SELECT needs_follow_up, COUNT(*) AS brackets, SUM(visits) AS visits FROM [C33 · Average cost by type of visit] GROUP BY needs_follow_up ORDER BY needs_follow_up

queries.name: F01 · Insurers of the patients of Madrid (IN with a subquery)
queries.description: IN with a subquery: the insurers whose identifier is used by a patient of Madrid.
queries.sql: SELECT id_insurer, name FROM insurers WHERE id_insurer IN (SELECT id_insurer FROM patients WHERE city = 'Madrid') ORDER BY id_insurer

queries.name: F02 · Drugs with no prescription (NOT IN with a subquery)
queries.description: NOT IN with a subquery: the drugs that no prescription uses.
queries.sql: SELECT id_drug, name FROM drugs WHERE id_drug NOT IN (SELECT id_drug FROM prescriptions) ORDER BY id_drug

queries.name: F03 · Specialties with no diagnosis (NOT IN with a subquery)
queries.description: The specialties that no diagnosis is linked to.
queries.sql: SELECT id_specialty, name FROM specialties WHERE id_specialty NOT IN (SELECT id_specialty FROM diagnoses) ORDER BY id_specialty

queries.name: F04 · Hospitals with an ICU room (EXISTS)
queries.description: EXISTS with a correlated subquery: it is checked again for every hospital.
queries.sql: SELECT h.id_hospital, h.name FROM hospitals AS h WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rooms AS r WHERE r.id_hospital = h.id_hospital AND r.type = 'ICU') ORDER BY h.id_hospital

queries.name: F05 · Hospitals with no ICU room (NOT EXISTS)
queries.description: The other side of the previous example: NOT EXISTS keeps the hospitals with no match.
queries.sql: SELECT h.id_hospital, h.name FROM hospitals AS h WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rooms AS r WHERE r.id_hospital = h.id_hospital AND r.type = 'ICU') ORDER BY h.id_hospital

queries.name: F06 · Patients with a high-risk surgery (EXISTS, correlated)
queries.description: The subquery points at the outer patient (p.id_patient): a correlated EXISTS.
queries.sql: SELECT p.id_patient, p.last_name FROM patients AS p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM surgeries AS s WHERE s.id_patient = p.id_patient AND s.risk = 'high') ORDER BY p.id_patient

queries.name: F07 · Dermatology doctors with more experience than some Cardiology doctor (> ANY)
queries.description: x > ANY (…) is true when the years beat at least one of the inner values.
queries.sql: SELECT id_doctor, last_name, years_experience FROM doctors WHERE id_specialty = 6 AND years_experience > ANY (SELECT years_experience FROM doctors WHERE id_specialty = 1) ORDER BY id_doctor

queries.name: F08 · The most experienced doctor of each specialty (>= ALL, correlated)
queries.description: x >= ALL (…) needs the comparison to hold for every inner value: only the top of each specialty passes.
queries.sql: SELECT d.id_doctor, d.last_name, d.years_experience FROM doctors AS d WHERE d.years_experience >= ALL (SELECT d2.years_experience FROM doctors AS d2 WHERE d2.id_specialty = d.id_specialty) ORDER BY d.id_specialty, d.id_doctor

queries.name: F09 · Chronic patients of a city with a private insurer (<> ALL)
queries.description: x <> ALL (…) is the same as x NOT IN (…): it keeps the values that differ from every one of them.
queries.sql: SELECT id_patient, last_name FROM patients WHERE is_chronic = TRUE AND id_insurer <> ALL (SELECT id_insurer FROM insurers WHERE type = 'public') ORDER BY id_patient

queries.name: F10 · University hospitals
queries.description: This query is not a test by itself: it is the view the next examples read inside a subquery.
queries.sql: SELECT id_hospital, name, city FROM hospitals WHERE is_university = TRUE

queries.name: F11 · Rooms of the university hospitals read from the view (subquery over a view)
queries.description: The subquery reads the view F10 as if it were a table: [F10 · …] inside the IN.
queries.sql: SELECT r.id_room, r.code FROM rooms AS r WHERE r.id_hospital IN (SELECT id_hospital FROM [F10 · University hospitals]) ORDER BY r.id_room

queries.name: F12 · Average cost per day of admissions of 700 or more (derived table)
queries.description: A subquery in the FROM with an alias (t) is a derived table: it is queried like any other table.
queries.sql: SELECT t.id_hospital, t.avg_cost FROM (SELECT r.id_hospital, AVG(a.cost_per_day) AS avg_cost FROM admissions AS a INNER JOIN rooms AS r ON r.id_room = a.id_room GROUP BY r.id_hospital) AS t WHERE t.avg_cost >= 700 ORDER BY t.id_hospital

queries.name: F13 · Hospitals with ten or more admissions (derived table and JOIN)
queries.description: The derived table is joined to the hospitals table and its column total is filtered.
queries.sql: SELECT t.id_hospital, h.name, t.total FROM (SELECT r.id_hospital, COUNT(*) AS total FROM admissions AS a INNER JOIN rooms AS r ON r.id_room = a.id_room GROUP BY r.id_hospital) AS t INNER JOIN hospitals AS h ON h.id_hospital = t.id_hospital WHERE t.total >= 10 ORDER BY t.total DESC, t.id_hospital

queries.name: F14 · Visits of every patient of a city (scalar subquery in SELECT)
queries.description: The subquery in the column list returns one value per row: the visits of that patient.
queries.sql: SELECT p.id_patient, p.last_name, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM visits AS v WHERE v.id_patient = p.id_patient) AS visits FROM patients AS p WHERE p.city = 'Bilbao' ORDER BY p.id_patient

queries.name: F15 · Admissions more expensive than the average (scalar subquery in WHERE)
queries.description: The subquery returns a single value (the average) that the WHERE compares with.
queries.sql: SELECT id_admission, cost_per_day FROM admissions WHERE cost_per_day > (SELECT AVG(cost_per_day) FROM admissions) ORDER BY id_admission

queries.name: F16 · Specialties with three or more diagnoses
queries.description: A query whose SQL carries a subquery also works as a view: this one uses a correlated EXISTS with HAVING.
queries.sql: SELECT s.id_specialty, s.name FROM specialties AS s WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM diagnoses AS d WHERE d.id_specialty = s.id_specialty HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3) ORDER BY s.id_specialty

queries.name: F17 · The previous view read as a table
queries.description: F16 is read from the FROM like a table, even though inside it there is a subquery.
queries.sql: SELECT id_specialty, name FROM [F16 · Specialties with three or more diagnoses] ORDER BY id_specialty

queries.name: F18 · Doctors of the specialties with a severe diagnosis (nested subqueries)
queries.description: One subquery inside another: the inner one picks the specialties and the outer one the doctors.
queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT d.id_doctor, d.last_name FROM doctors AS d WHERE d.id_specialty IN (SELECT id_specialty FROM diagnoses WHERE severity = 'severe') ORDER BY d.id_doctor

queries.name: F19 · Oncology doctors but the most experienced (NOT with ALL)
queries.description: NOT (… >= ALL (…)) is the negation of the ALL predicate: the whole specialty but its top doctor.
queries.sql: SELECT d.id_doctor, d.last_name, d.years_experience FROM doctors AS d WHERE d.id_specialty = 5 AND NOT (d.years_experience >= ALL (SELECT d2.years_experience FROM doctors AS d2 WHERE d2.id_specialty = 5)) ORDER BY d.id_doctor

queries.name: F20 · Rooms of the university hospitals (= ANY)
queries.description: x = ANY (…) is the same as x IN (…): it is kept for completeness of the quantifiers.
queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT r.id_hospital FROM rooms AS r WHERE r.id_hospital = ANY (SELECT id_hospital FROM hospitals WHERE is_university = TRUE) ORDER BY r.id_hospital

queries.name: F21 · Doctors with more experience than some Cardiology doctor (> SOME)
queries.description: SOME is a synonym of ANY: the comparison has to hold for at least one inner value.
queries.sql: SELECT id_doctor, last_name FROM doctors WHERE years_experience > SOME (SELECT years_experience FROM doctors WHERE id_specialty = 1) ORDER BY id_doctor

queries.name: G01 · Hospital and insurer names, without repeats
queries.description: UNION of two tables with one column each: the hospital names and the insurer names, every one once and sorted by name.
queries.sql: SELECT name FROM hospitals UNION SELECT name FROM insurers ORDER BY name

queries.name: G02 · The country of every hospital, twice (UNION ALL)
queries.description: The same SELECT on both sides of UNION ALL: the rows are stacked without removing repeats, so there are 14 of them.
queries.sql: SELECT country FROM hospitals UNION ALL SELECT country FROM hospitals ORDER BY country

queries.name: G03 · Every country once (UNION)
queries.description: The same union without ALL: UNION removes the repeated rows, so each country comes out once.
queries.sql: SELECT country FROM hospitals UNION SELECT country FROM hospitals ORDER BY country

queries.name: G04 · A union read as a table
queries.description: The union goes in the FROM with an alias (derived table): the doctor identifiers of the staff and of the appointments, without repeats, are counted.
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM (SELECT id_doctor FROM doctors UNION SELECT id_doctor FROM appointments) AS t

queries.name: G05 · Union with output alias, ORDER BY and LIMIT
queries.description: Both sides name their column item: the ORDER BY of the union sorts the combined result by that name and the LIMIT keeps the first 5.
queries.sql: SELECT name AS item FROM hospitals UNION SELECT name AS item FROM insurers ORDER BY item LIMIT 5

queries.name: H01 · Patients by city, read from the script
queries.description: Reads the result of the script “Patients by city” as if it were a table.
queries.sql: SELECT city, patients FROM [Patients by city] ORDER BY patients DESC, city

queries.name: H02 · How many cities the script returns
queries.description: Reads the result of the script “Patients by city” as if it were a table.
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM [Patients by city]

queries.name: H03 · Cities with 5 or more patients
queries.description: Reads the result of the script “Patients by city” as if it were a table.
queries.sql: SELECT city, patients FROM [Patients by city] WHERE patients >= 5 ORDER BY patients DESC, city
